title: Ethical AI for Young Digital Citizens: A Call to Action on Privacy Governance
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the problem of how artificial intelligence systems, including generative AI and other AI-driven digital platforms, create privacy, transparency, consent, and accountability risks for young digital citizens. The authors argue that current privacy regulations and AI governance approaches are largely reactive and adult-centric, leaving youth insufficiently protected in contexts where AI systems collect, infer, share, and monetize personal data.

Rather than testing a specific intervention, the paper proposes a stakeholder-centered governance and education framework for ethical AI privacy management. It synthesizes concerns from young people, parents, educators, AI professionals, and policymakers, and recommends privacy-by-design principles, age-appropriate consent practices, transparency statements, internal audits, independent oversight, and stronger regulatory standards. The paper also argues for integrating AI privacy education into school curricula and for training educators so they can guide students in responsible AI use.

The context is youth-facing AI across digital platforms and educational settings, with specific attention to schools in Canada and broader international regulatory examples such as GDPR, PIPEDA, and OPC guidance. The authors emphasize that educational institutions should adopt privacy education, student privacy audits, and multi-stakeholder collaboration, but the paper does not report an empirical school-based implementation study. Its main conclusion is that protecting young users requires coordinated governance, education, and technical safeguards that prioritize transparency, youth agency, and accountability.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A generic generative AI / large language model system used to generate or assist with text-based outputs and feedback in digital environments.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper discusses generative AI in the context of youth-facing digital platforms and educational tools, focusing on privacy governance, transparency, and safeguards rather than evaluating a specific product.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual call-to-action and policy paper, not an empirical evaluation of an AI tool. It presents literature-informed recommendations and governance principles without a primary study design, sample, or measured outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper argues for potentially important governance and privacy protections in education-related AI use, but it reports no measurable intervention effect. Because there are no outcome data, impact on student learning or school implementation cannot be determined from the paper.
